text:
Hello,

I'm writing about how the Talgrund Cooperative in Emmen got rid of me, and I'd be grateful for some guidance.

First, about my contract: there is nothing special in it about notice periods, no longer or shorter periods than normal, nothing like that. I checked it twice.

After I was sent home I wrote to Owen Foster, the manager, by e-mail on 23 February and asked him to give me the reasons for throwing me out in writing. I've attached the letter he sent back, and also one of my pay slips so you can see what I earned, CHF 1,140 a month for my part-time job in the cooperative's shop.

What happened is this. In early February I slipped on the ice on my way to work and hurt my knee badly. The doctor signed me off and I sent the certificate to the shop the same day. Tom Graf, who works with me, even drove me home from the clinic. When I came back on 21 February, Mr Foster told me I had been 'away far too much' and that the cooperative couldn't rely on me. The reason he gave was my absence, nothing else. But I didn't stay away because I wanted to, I couldn't walk.

He then said that was it: I was dismissed with immediate effect, from that very day, no notice period at all. I had to hand in my keys and leave.

The thing is, I was employed on a fixed-term contract from 1 May 2024 until 15 August 2026. We agreed that end date in writing when I started. By my count I'm losing about CHF 6,550 in wages up to that date.

Is this allowed? What should I do now?

Best regards,
Eva Hofer
Talstrasse 118, Emmen

Your employment certificate will follow by post.

Owen Foster
Manager
